tEn: Replit CEO Amjad Masad: What Young People Should Learn in the AI Era
tZh: Replit CEO Amjad Masad：AI 时代年轻人应该学什么
sEn: Replit CEO Amjad Masad argues that the true value of young people is to question deeply held beliefs and become heretics, and that college should foster first-principles thinking rather than prescribe what to learn.
sZh: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 认为，年轻人的真正价值在于质疑根深蒂固的观念、成为异端，大学应培养第一性原理思维，而非规定学习内容。

consensus.en: Young people's utility is to question deeply held beliefs and be heretics.
consensus.zh: 年轻人的价值在于质疑根深蒂固的信念，成为异端。

consensus.en: College should not be prescriptive; allow exploration, side quests, and project-based learning.
consensus.zh: 大学不应规定学习内容，应允许探索、支线任务和项目式学习。

consensus.en: AI enables customized, interest-driven learning for every student without rigid syllabi.
consensus.zh: AI 使每个学生都能进行定制化、兴趣驱动的学习，无需僵化教学大纲。

consensus.en: The future of companies will change; agents will enable true autonomy and self-driving organizations.
consensus.zh: 公司的未来将改变；智能体将实现真正的自主和自驱动组织。

consensus.en: Trust is crucial; Silicon Valley's high-trust ecosystem breeds amazing people and progress.
consensus.zh: 信任至关重要；硅谷的高信任生态孕育了杰出人才和进步。

consensus.en: Deeply following a thread and being able to teach something is most impressive in young talent.
consensus.zh: 深入钻研并能够传授知识，是年轻人才最令人印象深刻之处。

contrarian.en: Today's college beats outside thought out of students, opposite of its intended utility.
contrarian.zh: 当今大学扼杀学生的外部思考，与其应有价值背道而驰。

contrarian.en: Starting a startup at 18 is premature optimization; most teens should explore instead.
contrarian.zh: 18 岁创业是过早优化；大多数青少年应探索而非急于创业。

contrarian.en: VCs pre-committing teens with large checks is predatory, like the music industry.
contrarian.zh: 风投用大额支票预先锁定青少年是掠夺性的，如同音乐产业。

contrarian.en: You shouldn't learn to code anymore; AI will change how we build software.
contrarian.zh: 不应再学习编程；AI 将改变我们构建软件的方式。

contrarian.en: Holacracy failed due to technology, but AI agents can now make it work.
contrarian.zh: 合弄制因技术而失败，但 AI 智能体现在能使其可行。

contrarian.en: Trusting students to follow their own paths, even crazy ones, builds the future.
contrarian.zh: 信任学生走自己的路，即使疯狂，也能构建未来。

turns.en: Ultimately, the utility of young people is to question deeply held beliefs. It's to be heretics. And in today's college, it's actually the opposite. It kind of beats any outside thought out of them.
turns.zh: 归根结底，年轻人的用处就是质疑根深蒂固的信念。就是做异端。而今天的大学恰恰相反，它把任何外来的想法都从他们身上打掉。

turns.en: I just really want to see a world in which it's okay if you want to go on a side quest and go do something that's kind of oddball, but also might end up being super amazing if it works out.
turns.zh: 我真的想看到一个世界，在那里，如果你想去搞个支线任务，做点有点古怪的事，也没关系，而且如果成了，可能还会超级惊艳。

turns.en: The future of companies is going to change. The whole industry has changed. It's a complete reset on technology perspective.
turns.zh: 公司的未来将会改变。整个行业已经变了。从技术角度看，这是一次彻底的重置。

turns.en: I'd want to go to a college that is not prescriptive about what I learn. I'm motivated by what skills can it give me in order to achieve what I want to build.
turns.zh: 我想去一所不对我学什么指手画脚的大学。我关心的是它能给我什么技能，让我实现我想构建的东西。

turns.en: One of the core tenets of the academy side-steps this problem entirely. We don't care if you graduate or not. We don't have grades. We don't have tests. The amount of weight to push against should be a lot less.
turns.zh: 学院的一个核心原则完全绕开了这个问题。我们不在乎你毕不毕业。我们没有分数。我们没有考试。需要对抗的阻力应该小得多。

turns.en: When you see a 18-year-old that is really inspiring to you that you're like, I got to spend time with this person, what are they doing that is catching your interest?
turns.zh: 当你看到一个 18 岁的年轻人，让你觉得特别受启发，你会想“我得和这个人待一会儿”，他们做了什么吸引了你的兴趣？

turns.en: I think the first thing is that they As we were talking, uh I I remembered this uh sci-fi story that I read once. Uh it's called The City and the Stars. And it's about this future city that's governed by AGI. We sort of invented AGI. It now governs all of our lives. It solves all all problems, all human problems. Um there's no wars, there's uh no disease, everyone lives forever. And people spend their time working on like a thousand-year art projects and doing all sorts of random things to fill up their time. But they they found this problem where they accumulate so much knowledge and memory, it becomes like harder to keep it all in their heads. So, they invented this technology where they go into some kind of laboratory and they compress their memory. Sort of like context compression that we do with AI today. They go through all the memories and they compress them and then they go through a boot camp to like retrain them for for uh for for their life. So, they invented a new way to be born uh but it it is you're not fundamentally new person. You're still the same person. You're just editing your memory. But there's a glitch that happens in this system in this machine and there's a new person that is fundamentally born new. And he immediately starts causing problems. Uh in the boot camp he starts doing weird things, new things and everyone's like, "Whoa, that's that's crazy. Like you shouldn't be doing that. That's not how we do things." It becomes very disruptive. And then when they go out into into this like city, he starts asking questions like, "What's out there? What's in the stars? What's outside our city borders?" They're like, "Ah, we don't talk about outside our city borders."
turns.zh: 我觉得第一件事是，他们……我们刚才聊的时候，我想起我以前读过的一个科幻故事，叫《城市与群星》。它讲的是一个由 AGI 统治的未来城市。我们算是发明了 AGI，它现在管理着我们所有的生活，解决了所有问题，所有人类的问题。没有战争，没有疾病，每个人都永生。人们把时间花在千年艺术项目上，做各种随机的事情来填满时间。但他们发现了一个问题：他们积累了太多知识和记忆，越来越难全部装进脑子里。于是他们发明了一种技术，进入某种实验室压缩记忆。有点像我们今天对 AI 做的上下文压缩。他们遍历所有记忆，压缩它们，然后参加一个训练营，重新训练自己适应生活。所以他们发明了一种新的出生方式，但你本质上不是新人，你还是同一个人，只是在编辑记忆。但这个系统、这台机器出了个故障，一个全新的人诞生了。他立刻开始制造麻烦。在训练营里，他开始做奇怪的事、新的事，大家都说：“哇，这太疯狂了，你不该那样做，我们不是这样做的。”他变得非常具有破坏性。然后当他们进入城市，他开始问问题：“外面有什么？星星里有什么？我们城市边界之外是什么？”他们说：“啊，我们不谈城市边界之外的事。”

turns.en: Sounds like Silo almost.
turns.zh: 听起来几乎像《羊毛战记》。

turns.en: It's probably dangerous out there. Yeah, a little bit like Silo, a little bit like Fallout.
turns.zh: 外面可能很危险。是的，有点像《羊毛战记》，有点像《辐射》。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Um and and you know, I don't want to get into the spoilers too much but eventually that's what he has so much drive to change things and go discover the stars. That's why it's called the city in the stars. He in in in the story unfolds in that way and he finds all sorts of interesting things out there. And I'm reminded of this because as we're talking about what is college and what is it what is it for? And I I I think a a related question is like what is the utility of young people in society? And I think ultimately the utility of the young people is to question deeply held beliefs. Is to be heretics. Yeah and and today's college is actually the opposite. It kind of beats any outside thought out of them, right? It it it it it tells you you're stupid. We figured everything out. You need to learn our way and we need to prepare you for the outside world so you can get a job and be a perfect citizen and go get, you know, get married, have kids, and get a house and a car and and live happily ever after. But that world doesn't exist anymore. You can do really well in college and you can still be unemployed with a huge debt. Um but not only that, I think that the the real civilizational missing opportunity is is that is is that person in the city of the stars. It took a glitch to get someone with a clear mind to be able to question deeply held beliefs. And you know, every one of us, we probably have a blind spots in society. We We have a lot of blind spots in Silicon Valley. There's a lot of ideas that don't come out of Silicon Valley uh because there's a monoculture here. There's a certain way of thinking. Every culture is somehow a monoculture, even the most radical cultures like Silicon Valley. And so what what do you need from young people? You need them to um to experiment. You need to encourage them to do to try impossible things and every now and then they're going to have a breakthrough that once we thought was impossible and now it's now it's suddenly possible because the technology changed, something changed. Um so college ultimately should be about that. Let's get these these people with clear minds, Zen mindsets, first principle mindsets and encourage them to go question the deeply held beliefs.
turns.zh: 嗯，你知道，我不想剧透太多，但最终他有着巨大的动力去改变事物、去发现星辰。这就是为什么叫《城市与群星》。故事就这样展开，他在外面发现了各种有趣的东西。我之所以想起这个，是因为我们在讨论什么是大学、大学是为了什么？我觉得一个相关的问题是：年轻人在社会中的用处是什么？我认为归根结底，年轻人的用处就是质疑根深蒂固的信念，就是做异端。而今天的大学恰恰相反，它把任何外来的想法都从他们身上打掉，对吧？它告诉你你很蠢。我们什么都搞明白了。你需要学我们的方式，我们需要为你进入外部世界做准备，这样你就能找到工作，成为完美公民，然后结婚、生子、买房、买车，从此幸福地生活。但那个世界已经不存在了。你可以在大学里表现很好，但仍然失业，还背着一大笔债。不仅如此，我认为真正错失的文明机会，就是《城市与群星》里的那个人。需要一个故障才能让一个头脑清晰的人去质疑根深蒂固的信念。你知道，我们每个人可能都有社会盲点。我们在硅谷有很多盲点。很多想法不是从硅谷出来的，因为这里有一种单一文化。有一种特定的思维方式。每种文化在某种程度上都是单一文化，即使像硅谷这样最激进的文化也是如此。那么你需要年轻人做什么？你需要他们去实验。你需要鼓励他们去尝试不可能的事，偶尔他们会取得突破，曾经我们认为不可能的事，现在突然可能了，因为技术变了，某些东西变了。所以大学最终应该围绕这个。让我们把这些头脑清晰、有禅宗心态、第一性原理思维的人聚集起来，鼓励他们去质疑根深蒂固的信念。

turns.en: Yeah, I I think that's well said. I mean, imagine if you were 18 today and you were at, you know, were able to design your ideal experience in terms of, you know, how much you go to class, to what projects you work on, to what kind of deep study you would engage in, to what you'd want to study. What are some principles or, you know, that you would add to that in terms of how you wish, if you could redo, you know, 18 to 22, but in 2026?
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得你说得很好。想象一下，如果你今天 18 岁，能够设计你理想的大学体验，比如上多少课、做什么项目、进行什么样的深度学习、想学什么。你会加入哪些原则？如果你能重来 18 到 22 岁，但是在 2026 年，你会怎么想？

turns.en: How you think about it?
turns.zh: 你会怎么考虑？

turns.en: Yeah, I I I'd want to go to a college that's not prescriptive about what I learn. I want to be I I want to be an environment where there's a lot of different paths. Like, you know, there is there's a class about something totally I haven't even thought about. It's outside my world, right? We're talking about the story with um Steve Jobs, one of the most inspiring speeches he gave is the Stanford commencement speech. And he talked about connecting things backwards. So, the way Steve Jobs approached college, I think it's the ideal experience of college. Where he's like, he went to Reed College, but he couldn't afford it, so he dropped out, but kept dropping into different classes. One of them was calligraphy. And in the calligraphy class, he didn't know why he was interested in it, and he just did it and learned it. Later on, when they were inventing the Mac, inventing user interfaces, they're like, "Oh, we should have proportionally spaced fonts. We should have certain people should be able to
turns.zh: 是的，我想去一所不对我学什么指手画脚的大学。我想成为一个有很多不同路径的环境。比如，有一门课是关于我完全没想到的东西，它在我世界之外，对吧？我们谈到史蒂夫·乔布斯的故事，他最鼓舞人心的演讲之一是在斯坦福毕业典礼上的演讲。他谈到了连点成线。所以，乔布斯对待大学的方式，我认为是理想的大学体验。他去了里德学院，但付不起学费，所以退学了，但继续旁听不同的课。其中一门是书法课。在书法课上，他不知道为什么感兴趣，就只是去学。后来，当他们发明 Mac、发明用户界面时，他们说：“哦，我们应该有比例间距字体。我们应该让某些人能够

turns.en: select fonts.
turns.zh: 选择字体。

turns.zh: 而这直接呼应了他大学时代学习字体、书法之类的东西。

turns.en: And so, this meandering that I think modern society thinks is sort of useless, I think it's actually the most useful in college. Can you take a class that would change the direction of your life because you discovered something totally new and outside of your world? So that's one. I would like to have enough freedom to select the kind of things I want to study.
turns.zh: 这种漫无目的的探索，现代社会觉得没什么用，但我认为在大学里恰恰是最有用的。你能不能上一门课，就因为你发现了某个全新的、完全在你世界之外的东西，从而改变你人生的方向？所以这是第一点。我希望能有足够的自由去选择我想学的东西。

turns.en: The other thing is, if I am engrossed in building something, give me the space and time to do it. One of the things about my college that was really hard is we had attendance. They counted attendance, and if you didn't attend for like six classes, you were banned. And so I think if I'm going to school, I'm doing all these different things, I'm meeting interesting people, and then I have an idea and I'm manically working really hard, give me the space to do it. Don't expel me from—
turns.zh: 另一点是，如果我正全身心投入在做某件事，请给我空间和时间去做。我大学里特别难受的一点就是有考勤。他们统计出勤，如果你缺了大概六节课，就会被禁。所以我觉得，如果我在上学，我在做各种不同的事，我在认识有趣的人，然后我有了一个想法，我疯狂地拼命工作，那就给我空间去做。别把我开除——

turns.en: Don't yank my—
turns.zh: 别把我拽走——

turns.en: Yeah, exactly. For sure.
turns.zh: 对，没错。当然。

turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: And finally, the quality of people. I think if you're around conventionally minded people, eventually you'll be conventionally minded.
turns.zh: 最后一点，是人的质量。我觉得如果你身边都是思维循规蹈矩的人，最终你也会变得循规蹈矩。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: If you're in an environment that encourages people to question those deeply held beliefs, I think you will be able to do that.
turns.zh: 如果你处在一个鼓励人们质疑那些根深蒂固信念的环境里，我觉得你就能做到这一点。

But one of the things that I really enjoyed was that there was actually no expectation of attending class for most situations. And so I had many semesters where I had like three jobs in one semester. And often the time that I was expected to be at work overlapped with my class.
turns.zh: 对。我上的是加州大学伯克利分校，Go Bears，我确实非常享受。但让我特别喜欢的一点是，大多数情况下其实并没有必须到课的期望。所以我有很多学期，一个学期打三份工。而且经常我该上班的时间跟我的课是冲突的。

turns.en: Mhm.

turns.en: So I just looked at my midterm schedule the semester in advance and I said, "Okay, these are my two midterms. Hey boss, can I take those two days off?" And otherwise I was working.
turns.zh: 所以我就提前看那个学期的期中考试安排，我说：“好，我就这两场期中考试。老板，我能请那两天假吗？”除此之外我都在工作。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: But it's interesting because now I look back and I did enjoy that, but I feel often times I look at that experience and say, "Well, what if the environment was supportive of this?"
turns.zh: 但有意思的是，现在回头看，我确实享受那段经历，可我常常看着那段经历想：“如果当时的环境是支持这种做法的，会怎样？”

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Like, what would happen if—because honestly, I think today, when I talk to students, it's been 20 years plus, when I talk to students today, they all do this. This used to be odd, my behavior. And now it's becoming the norm. And the thing that's weird though is that it's not encouraged yet. It's still not allowed. turns.zh: 比如，如果——因为说实话，我觉得今天，当我跟学生聊天时，已经过去二十多年了，今天我跟学生聊天，他们都在这么做。我以前这种行为算是古怪的。现在它正在变成常态。但奇怪的是，它还没有被鼓励。它仍然不被允许。所以对我个人来说，我真的很想看到一个世界：你想去搞个支线任务，去做点有点古怪的事，但如果成了可能会超级惊艳，这也没关系。

turns.en: Be able to use the college resources. You should be able to use the computer lab, the computes, the bio lab, whatever it is.
turns.zh: 能用上大学的资源。你应该能用计算机实验室、算力、生物实验室，不管是什么。

turns.en: You shouldn't be going against the grain. It should be like actually actively encouraging you. Actually, they should be bringing resources to you more if you do it.
turns.zh: 你不该是在逆流而行。学校应该主动鼓励你。实际上，如果你这么做，他们更应该把资源送到你面前。

turns.en: Yeah.

turns.en: So, like, if you have a crazy idea that's taking off, the college—you shouldn't be hiding it from your college. They should be coming like, "Oh my god. This is amazing. Let's give them more."
turns.zh: 所以，如果你有个疯狂的想法正在起飞，大学——你不该瞒着你的大学。他们应该主动过来：“天哪。这太棒了。多给他们点资源。”

turns.en: Totally. There's this kid Eric, I think he's Richard's friend, who has to take investor calls from the bathroom because he's hiding in the school. Yeah, they should be like coaching him through it or enabling it in some way. Bringing investor demo day or something. You know, this kind of thing.
turns.zh: 完全同意。有个孩子叫 Eric，我想他是 Richard 的朋友，他得躲在学校的厕所里接投资人的电话。对，学校应该辅导他走过这个过程，或者以某种方式支持他。办个投资人 Demo Day 之类的。你懂的，这种事。

turns.en: A couple comments. One is going back to your thing around calligraphy, you know, people get these interests that might seem random and might be random, but in other ways might tie back in other ways. And I think there actually ways in which the school can sort of develop—it's hard to force natural interest. And so, for example, I was obsessed with basketball as a kid. But I was also the kid who would ask my math teacher like, "What's the point of this? Help explain it to me." And if she could have explained it to me, maybe I would have got excited about it. If she would say, "Hey, you know, you're obsessed with basketball, you need to understand the salary cap, or actually basketball is very analytical now in terms of people are using stats and data to evaluate players. And so, if you don't understand this, you're not going to be a good student of the game." That would have got me really excited. That's what I'm so excited about Alpha School. Is the way that they take people's natural interests and get them to learn things that they're going to need to know over time out of that.
turns.zh: 我有几点评论。一是回到你提到的书法，人们会产生一些看起来随机、可能也确实是随机的兴趣，但在其他方面又可能以别的方式关联回来。我觉得学校其实有办法去培养——强行制造自然兴趣很难。举个例子，我小时候痴迷篮球。但我也是那种会问数学老师“这有什么意义？帮我解释一下”的孩子。如果她能给我解释清楚，也许我就会对它兴奋起来。如果她说：“嘿，你痴迷篮球，你需要理解工资帽，或者其实篮球现在非常分析化，人们用统计和数据来评估球员。所以如果你不懂这个，你就不会是个好的比赛研究者。”那会让我非常兴奋。这就是我对 Alpha School 如此兴奋的原因。他们能把人们自然的兴趣，转化成去学习那些他们迟早需要知道的东西。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: The thing that's so hard is we all know the education—sort of the academic, the industry of education if you will, or the academic canon of education—is completely on board with this. They totally understand that it would be great if every student could have a customized curriculum. And Joe Lehman of Alpha School talks about this all the time. The problem is that practically it seems impossible. turns.zh: 让我用不同的方式来表达，

turns.zh: 是的。

turns.zh: 是的，真的很有趣。这肯定是个支线任务，对吧？是个支线任务。比如，它怎么会相关呢？实际上，我认为它在很多方面帮助了我的商业。这些技能在两个方向上都非常可转移。但最有趣的事情之一是认识到信任有多么宝贵。如果你在整个社会中有一个信任的基础，它会多么大地改变你前进的方式。在地方政治中，举个简单的例子，让我们谈谈非营利组织。如果你经营一个非营利组织，你从某人那里筹集资金，你与他们交谈，他们说：“我会给你 5 万美元。”那 5 万美元最终到达你银行账户的可能性大约在 20% 到 50% 之间。

turns.zh: 在他们口头承诺之后，对吧？所以，口头承诺没有分量。在硅谷，我认为可能是 75% 到 100%，取决于你在和谁说话以及你是谁。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And the difference in how you operate—like I can confidently continue to move forward on my business if I know that the money's coming. turns.zh: 以及你运作方式的差异——比如，如果我知道钱会来，我可以自信地继续推进我的业务。然后等你交付支票时，我已经取得了大约 6 周的进展，对吧？现在突然之间，你的支票在 6 周后更有价值了。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: And the reverse is also true. If you do not have trust, then all of a sudden, you're like, "Well, what if this donor is upset about this thing? Let me do this thing differently." turns.zh: 反之亦然。如果你没有信任，那么突然之间，你会想：“嗯，如果这个捐赠者对这件事不满怎么办？让我换个方式做这件事。”但你没有履行你的使命。你担心。你对这件事感到焦虑和压力。所以我认为这是硅谷提供的东西，可以应用到学校。

turns.en: In what way?
turns.zh: 以什么方式？

turns.en: Trusting students to do what they want to do and follow the threads they want to do is something that I think we can uniquely offer. I think that Silicon Valley is a place where someone who has a unique idea or a different way of doing things can generally be accepted and allowed to do it. Now, there are some social rules. Like you can't just go around being mean to everyone or lying or it's not that, you know, it's not that permissive, you know. But if we start trusting young kids and young adults to go and follow what they want and then we empower them, even if we think what they're doing is crazy, then they're going to build that future you're talking about. They're going to figure out the next version of holacracy that actually works.
turns.zh: 信任学生去做他们想做的事，追随他们想追随的线索，这是我认为我们可以独特提供的东西。我认为硅谷是一个地方，一个有独特想法或不同做事方式的人通常可以被接受并允许去做。现在，有一些社会规则。比如你不能到处对每个人刻薄或撒谎，不是那样的，你知道，不是那么宽容。但如果我们开始信任年幼的孩子和年轻人去追随他们想要的，然后我们赋予他们权力，即使我们认为他们做的事情很疯狂，那么他们就会建立你所说的那个未来。他们会找出真正有效的下一版 holacracy。

turns.zh: 让我问你一个问题。这可能有点棘手，但你会怎么处理那些捣乱的人？就像总会有一些人会破坏东西。比如，你知道，扎克伯格著名的 Facemash，那真的很有争议。比如我黑进了我们的——有人可能听说过它拼写为——

turns.zh: 是的，你怎么看？我的意思是，显然有些事情真的越过了某种犯罪红线，但比如——

So, there's no question, like if you do something like violate our sexual harassment policy or, you know, you are super mean to someone in front of everyone, you know, like there are going to be rules, of course. Like, we have to create a culture of trust and positive sum.
turns.zh: 哦，当然。是的，我的意思是，明确一点，你必须在某处划清界限，对吧？所以，毫无疑问，比如如果你做了违反我们性骚扰政策的事情，或者，你知道，你在所有人面前对某人非常刻薄，你知道，当然会有规则。比如，我们必须创造一种信任和正和的文化。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.zh: 同时，我认为学院的核心原则之一完全绕过了这个问题。

turns.zh: 我们没有分数。我们没有考试。那种要对抗的压力应该小得多。因此，很多这些挑战，人们做的事情，就像你想建 Face Smash，去吧。我的意思是，谁在乎呢，对吧？比如我愿意捍卫你这样做的权利。如果有人让我在播客上说：“是的，那是个奇怪的想法。”我也很高兴。比如，我不知道那个孩子在做什么。我不喜欢它，但你知道吗？他们必须做他们必须做的事。人们就是这样。所以我会说同样的话：如果你创造一个信任的环境，如果你允许这种情况发生，并且你设计得让他们没有一种反权威的心态，那么我认为你打开了很多创造力和很多机会。

turns.zh: 嗯，是的，这很有意思。我觉得回到你提到的，什么时候该信任长辈，什么时候该颠覆，这其实有一个普遍的趋势，就是真正重要的是获得辨别力，因为所有规则和启发式方法，其实都取决于具体情境和个案。而获得辨别力的方式就是通过反复练习。嗯，要信任学生，让他们自己失败、做决定、从中学习。你在这个播客里创造了“技术积极主义”这个词。我要创造的是“元最大化”。

turns.zh: 我我我认为在这里拥有一个好人的声誉实际上是非常有价值的。人们信任你管理他们的钱，信任你管理公司等等。我认为在大学里培养这种意识非常重要。我认为成为一个适应良好的人很重要。嗯，我知道有一段时间，有些人扮演这种自闭症天才的角色。也许在某个时候这很管用。我记得红杉资本关于 SBF 的博客文章，那简直是金句。他们删了。你可以在 archive.org 上找到。我认为这不再管用了。我认为硅谷不再是这种叛逆的东西。我们是一种机构。它已经是建制的一部分了。嗯，我们还必须与世界对接，对吧？人们需要明白我们有责任，我们不仅仅是在自己人之间说话。我们说的话，比如伯尼·桑德斯读了 Dwarkesh 的博客文章。我批评了 Dwarkesh 的那种语言，那些不懂这项技术的人，他们不会……那篇博客文章，在我看来，并没有让他们更理解。实际上，如果你不懂，你可能会从中学到错误的教训。所以我认为重要的是，我们创建或这个学院培养出适应良好的成年人，他们不仅能说内部语言，这很重要，但最终能站在国会面前。嗯，最后，关于价值观的培养，或者成为好人的想法，你还有什么想说的吗？你觉得学校或学校环境对此有贡献吗？我们提到过伟大的书籍。教一些这些东西会很好。我花了很多时间自学伦理和道德。
